findings.evidence: Container: toast; Placement: in a dialog centered on the password reset step, over the new password field it blocks
findings.fix: Present this message in a persistent modal or inline block that stays until the reader acts, not a toast that clears on its own.
findings.violation: The failure is fully blocking, the reader cannot continue the password reset at all until they request a new link, yet it is presented as a self-clearing toast, so a reader who looks away misses the one message explaining why the field is unusable.

findings.evidence: This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again.
findings.fix: Add a brief reason for the 30-character maximum, e.g. "This field takes a maximum of 30 characters, the most the shipping label can print. Shorten the entry and save again."
findings.violation: The message states a limit the product itself sets with no reason attached, and the reader will meet the same limit again anywhere they enter a long value in this field, so knowing why it exists would change how they approach retyping it.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Add a brief acknowledgment before the instruction, e.g. "Sorry, your last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for help restoring them."
findings.violation: The failure is total and unrecoverable in the moment (Suggested fix is none, no other message block on this screen offers a way forward, and the message reports a completed, unrecoverable loss), yet the wording is a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what the loss costs the reader.

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code, a code-style token, or an engineering-jargon term standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read. Change this file to one of those formats and upload it again, or select a different receipt.
findings.fix: Check the file's format at selection time and warn immediately if it is not PDF or PNG, rather than waiting until submit.
findings.violation: The mistake is marked predictable and the message fires only on-submit, with nothing earlier in the flow warning the reader, even though the file's format is knowable the moment it is selected, before the form is ever submitted.

findings.evidence: Placement: at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, though the field itself stays visible on the page
findings.fix: Move the password requirement message to directly below the password field, beside the field's own validation state.
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a long form rather than beside or below the password field it concerns, requiring the reader to scroll away from the field to read it.
